senses.definition: Happening, done, or needed every day.
senses.example: We keep a daily record of the weather.

senses.definition: Every day.
senses.example: The pool opens daily at noon.

senses.definition: Harm to something that makes it work less well or look worse.
senses.example: The spilled juice did some damage to the paper map.

senses.definition: To harm or spoil something.
senses.example: The heavy bag could damage the thin shelf.

senses.definition: To move your body in a pattern, often with music.
senses.example: We like to dance when our favorite song comes on.

senses.definition: A set of movements performed to music, or an event where people do them.
senses.example: My uncle taught me a dance from his school days.

senses.definition: The chance that someone will be hurt or something will be harmed.
senses.example: The warning flag tells swimmers there may be danger.

senses.definition: To be willing to do something difficult or scary.
senses.example: Would you dare to sing on a stage?

senses.definition: To challenge someone to try something hard or risky.
senses.example: My friend dared me to finish the puzzle before the bell.

senses.definition: A challenge to do something difficult or scary.
senses.example: Trying the sour candy was a silly dare.

senses.definition: Having little or no light, or close to black in color.
senses.example: The path was dark after the sun went down.

senses.definition: The time or space where there is little or no light.
senses.example: We could hear frogs calling after dark.

senses.definition: To move very quickly for a short time.
senses.example: We dashed indoors when it began to rain.

senses.definition: A quick run or a short race.
senses.example: I made a dash for the bus.

senses.definition: A small amount of something added to food or drink.
senses.example: Dad added a dash of cinnamon to the apples.

senses.definition: A line used as a mark in writing.
senses.example: The teacher put a dash on the board to show where a thought broke off.

senses.definition: Information such as measurements, counts, or answers gathered to help you learn about something.
senses.example: We collected data on how much rain fell each day.

senses.definition: An organized set of information that a program can search and use.
senses.example: We searched a database for books written by the same person.

senses.definition: A day, month, and sometimes year that tell when something happens.
senses.example: Write today’s date at the top of the page.

senses.definition: A planned meeting, sometimes with someone you like in a romantic way.
senses.example: My parents went on a dinner date.

senses.definition: A sweet, soft fruit that grows on certain palm trees.
senses.example: I put a date and a few almonds in my snack box.

senses.definition: To write or determine when something happened or was made.
senses.example: The artist did not date the picture.

senses.definition: The time when light first appears in the morning.
senses.example: At dawn, the birds began to call.

senses.definition: To begin to grow light, or to begin to be understood.
senses.example: It dawned on me that I had read the wrong page.

senses.definition: A pleasant thought or story you imagine while awake.
senses.example: My daydream was about exploring an island.

senses.definition: To let your mind wander into imagined thoughts while you are awake.
senses.example: I like to daydream on long car rides.

senses.definition: An agreement or arrangement made between people.
senses.example: We made a deal to trade chores on Wednesdays.

senses.definition: To give out cards for a game.
senses.example: Please deal five cards to each player.

senses.definition: To handle or do something about a person, problem, or situation.
senses.example: The class had to deal with a leak in the ceiling.

senses.definition: Loved or valued very much.
senses.example: I have known my dear friend since kindergarten.

senses.definition: Used before a person’s name at the start of a letter or email.
senses.example: I began my letter with “Dear Aunt May.”

senses.definition: A planned discussion where people give reasons for different views.
senses.example: Our class held a debate about where to put the new garden.

senses.definition: To talk or think about different sides of an issue before deciding.
senses.example: We debated which poster would be easiest to read.

senses.definition: Money or something else that a person or group owes.
senses.example: I used part of my allowance to pay back my debt to my brother.

senses.definition: To find and fix problems in a program or another system.
senses.example: We stopped to debug the instructions when the score went the wrong way.

senses.definition: To choose what you will do or what you think is best.
senses.example: We must decide which game to play before lunch.

senses.definition: Describes a tree or shrub that drops most of its leaves for part of each year.
senses.example: The deciduous maple was bare in winter.

senses.definition: A number written with a decimal point and one or more digits to its right, such as 2.75.
senses.example: The decimal 0.5 is another way to write one half.

senses.definition: Using a system based on ten and its place values.
senses.example: Our decimal number system groups ten ones into one ten.

senses.definition: The dot that separates the ones place from the smaller places in a number.
senses.example: In 2.5, the decimal point comes before the five.

senses.definition: A choice made after thinking about what to do.
senses.example: My decision was to take the shorter route home.

senses.definition: A living thing that breaks dead material into simpler substances.
senses.example: A fungus can act as a decomposer after a branch falls.

senses.definition: To add color, pictures, or other things to make something look special.
senses.example: We used paper circles to decorate the door.

senses.definition: To become smaller or make something smaller in amount, number, or size.
senses.example: Turning the knob left will decrease the volume.

senses.definition: A drop in amount, size, or number.
senses.example: We saw a decrease in the number of people waiting.

senses.definition: An action a person does, often one remembered as good or bad.
senses.example: Her kind deed made a hard day easier.

senses.definition: A document showing certain rights to property, such as land or a house.
senses.example: My grandmother keeps the deed to her house in a safe.

senses.definition: Going far down from the top or far in from the surface.
senses.example: The pond gets deep near the middle.

senses.definition: Low in sound or strong and dark in color.
senses.example: The drum made a deep sound.

senses.definition: Strong or serious, as a feeling or thought.
senses.example: We took a deep interest in the old maps.

senses.definition: A hoofed animal with long legs. In many kinds, the males grow pointed, branching antlers each year.
senses.example: Two deer stood quietly at the edge of the woods.

senses.definition: To win against someone or something in a contest or struggle.
senses.example: Our team hoped to defeat the champions.

senses.definition: A loss in a game, contest, or struggle.
senses.example: We took our defeat well and thanked the other team.

senses.definition: To protect someone or something, or give reasons why an idea is right.
senses.example: The goalie worked hard to defend the net.

senses.definition: To explain what a word, phrase, or idea means.
senses.example: Can you define the word in the first sentence?

senses.definition: Without doubt, or in a way that is sure.
senses.example: I will definitely bring my library card tomorrow.

senses.definition: A unit used to measure an angle or a temperature.
senses.example: A full turn is 360 degrees.

senses.definition: To make something happen later than planned.
senses.example: The rain may delay the start of the game.

senses.definition: A wait or a change that makes something happen later than planned.
senses.example: A bridge repair caused a short delay on the bus ride.

senses.definition: To take something to a person or place where it is expected.
senses.example: The mail carrier will deliver the package to our door.

senses.definition: To give a talk, message, or performance.
senses.example: A student will deliver the welcome speech.

senses.definition: An area of land built from sand, mud, or other material dropped by a river near its mouth.
senses.example: The river split into several channels as it flowed across its delta.

senses.definition: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as Δ or δ.
senses.example: The uppercase delta looks like a triangle.

senses.definition: To ask strongly for something or need it in order to happen.
senses.example: Building the kite demanded patience.

senses.definition: A strong request, or how much people want to use or buy something.
senses.example: There was high demand for seats at the show.

senses.definition: The bottom number in a fraction, showing how many equal parts make one whole.
senses.example: In 3/4, the denominator is 4.

senses.definition: How much matter is packed into a given amount of space. A small block of metal is usually denser than a wooden block of the same size.
senses.example: The oil rose above the water because it had a lower density.

senses.definition: To say that something is not true, or refuse to give something someone asks for.
senses.example: I could not deny that my footprints were on the clean floor.

senses.definition: To need or count on someone or something.
senses.example: Many birds depend on trees for shelter.

senses.definition: To be decided or changed by a condition or event.
senses.example: Our picnic plans depend on the weather.

senses.definition: The ability to notice how far away things are or which objects are nearer than others.
senses.example: Depth perception helps me tell which branch is closer.

senses.definition: To tell what someone or something is like.
senses.example: Can you describe the bird you saw?

senses.definition: A region with very little rain or snow over time.
senses.example: Some plants in the desert store water in their stems.

senses.definition: To leave a person, group, or place that depends on you.
senses.example: The story’s hero would not desert a friend in trouble.

senses.definition: A weather pattern that brings very little rain or snow over a long time.
senses.example: The desert climate was dry even when snow fell in winter.

senses.definition: A plan or pattern for how something will look or work.
senses.example: The students chose a simple design for the poster.

senses.definition: To make that plan or pattern.
senses.example: We will design a lamp that can stand on a narrow shelf.

senses.definition: A dish, often sweet, eaten at the end of a meal.
senses.example: I chose a peach for dessert.

senses.definition: One small part of a larger thing or piece of information.
senses.example: She remembered one detail about the dog: its red collar.

senses.definition: To describe something by giving its parts or facts.
senses.example: The note detailed when and where we should meet.

senses.definition: A cleaning product that helps water remove dirt or grease.
senses.example: We put laundry detergent in the washing machine.

senses.definition: To grow or change over time, or to help something new take shape.
senses.example: The class will develop a plan for the spring concert.

senses.definition: A feature that asks for proof that you are allowed to use a device before it opens.
senses.example: I put on the device lock before I left the tablet on the table.

senses.definition: The temperature to which air must cool before water vapor begins to turn into drops, if the amount of water in the air stays the same.
senses.example: The grass cooled to the dew point and tiny drops formed.

senses.definition: Going at a slant, like a line from one corner of a square to the opposite corner.
senses.example: The checker made a diagonal move.

senses.definition: A way a group of people uses a language. It can have its own sounds, words, and ways of putting words together.
senses.example: The two friends spoke different dialects of English and understood each other.

senses.definition: Words spoken back and forth between people or characters.
senses.example: Actors practiced the dialogue from the first page.

senses.definition: A straight line passing through the center of a circle from one edge to the other, or the length of that line.
senses.example: We measured the diameter of the plate by holding a ruler across its center.

senses.definition: The broad muscle below your lungs that helps you breathe.
senses.example: The diaphragm moves down to make room for the lungs to fill with air.

senses.definition: A way two things are not the same.
senses.example: The main difference is that my bag has two pockets.

senses.definition: The amount left when one number is taken away from another.
senses.example: The difference between nine and four is five.

senses.definition: Hard to do, understand, or deal with.
senses.example: It was difficult to hear the speaker from the back of the hall.

senses.definition: The way your body breaks food down into small parts it can take in and use.
senses.example: Chewing and mixing food with saliva start digestion.

senses.definition: One of the symbols used to write a number, such as 0, 1, or 2.
senses.example: The number 73 has two digits.

senses.definition: The main meal of the day, often eaten in the evening.
senses.example: We set the table for dinner.

senses.definition: The way in which someone or something moves, points, or faces.
senses.example: The arrow shows the direction of the exit.

senses.definition: An instruction that tells where to go or what to do.
senses.example: Please read each direction before starting the game.

senses.definition: To have a different idea or opinion from someone else.
senses.example: We disagree about the best way to build the tower.

senses.definition: To go out of sight or stop being present.
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared into the bushes.

senses.definition: To make someone feel sad because things did not go as hoped.
senses.example: The change in plans may disappoint the players.

senses.definition: To find or learn something you did not know before.
senses.example: We discovered a second path down to the pond.

senses.definition: To talk about a subject and share ideas or information.
senses.example: The group will discuss the first chapter tomorrow.

senses.definition: To spread through another material in particles so small that you no longer see the separate pieces.
senses.example: The sugar began to dissolve in the water.

senses.definition: How far it is from one point to another.
senses.example: We measured the distance from the door to the gate.

senses.definition: A rule that lets you multiply the parts of a sum or difference separately, then put the results back together.
senses.example: By the distributive property, four times 12 equals four times ten plus four times two.

senses.definition: To separate something into parts or groups.
senses.example: Divide the crayons between the two tables.

senses.definition: In math, to find the size of equal groups or how many times one number fits into another.
senses.example: If you divide twelve by three, you get four.

senses.definition: The long material carrying inherited information that many cells keep and use.
senses.example: The cell holds much of its DNA in a nucleus.

senses.definition: To act, work on a task, or carry it out.
senses.example: I will do the dishes after the game.

senses.definition: A word used before another action word to make some questions, negatives, or strong statements.
senses.example: Do you like puzzles? I do like them!

senses.definition: A readable name used to identify a place or group of places on a network.
senses.example: Two pages on the site can share a domain name.

senses.definition: A round roof or ceiling that curves upward like part of a ball.
senses.example: Sunlight streamed in through windows under the dome.

senses.definition: A small playing tile usually marked into two halves, each with a number of dots.
senses.example: I matched a domino with five dots at the end of the row.

senses.definition: A fin that rises from the back of a swimming animal.
senses.example: The orca’s dorsal fin showed above the water.

senses.definition: A graph that shows data by placing dots over the matching marks on a number line.
senses.example: Our dot plot had two dots over nine because two leaves were that length.

senses.definition: Twice as much or made with two parts.
senses.example: We need a double batch of muffins today.

senses.definition: To make or become twice as much.
senses.example: We will double the time from five minutes to ten.

senses.definition: A person who looks very much like another person, or who takes an actor’s place in a scene.
senses.example: A stunt double climbed the wall for the actor.

senses.definition: A feeling of being unsure that something is true or will happen.
senses.example: I had some doubt about whether the gate would be open.

senses.definition: To feel unsure or think something may not be true.
senses.example: I doubt that the little box can hold a bowling ball.

senses.definition: A force from a fluid such as air or water that opposes movement through it.
senses.example: Drag made it harder to ride my bike into the wind.

senses.definition: A line of high ground that separates areas where water flows toward different streams, lakes, or other places.
senses.example: Rain ran toward different creeks on the two sides of the drainage divide.

senses.definition: A story written to be acted, or a type of story with serious events.
senses.example: The class watched a short drama about a missing letter.

senses.definition: A situation with strong feelings or surprises.
senses.example: There was drama when the little dog escaped just before the show.

senses.definition: To make a picture, shape, or line by marking a surface.
senses.example: Let’s draw a map of the park.

senses.definition: To pull something in a direction or get something from a place.
senses.example: I will draw a name from the hat.

senses.definition: A game or contest that ends without a winner.
senses.example: Neither team scored, so the match ended in a draw.

senses.definition: To be unable to remember or think of the thing you are looking for.
senses.example: I knew the dog’s name yesterday, but today I draw a blank every time.

senses.definition: Images and events your mind makes while you sleep.
senses.example: I had a dream about a talking bike.

senses.definition: Something you strongly hope will happen.
senses.example: Her dream is to play the violin in a concert.

senses.definition: To have a dream or imagine something you want.
senses.example: My brother dreams of visiting a desert.

senses.definition: To control a ball while moving, such as by bouncing it in basketball or with small kicks in soccer.
senses.example: Maya learned to dribble a basketball with either hand.

senses.definition: To let a liquid run in a thin trickle or a few little drops.
senses.example: The rain began to dribble down the window.

senses.definition: To move slowly without much control or effort.
senses.example: We watched leaves drift across the pond.

senses.definition: A pile of snow, sand, or other material gathered by wind or water.
senses.example: A drift of snow blocked the back door.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
senses.example: I stopped to drink some water after the race.

senses.definition: A liquid that people can swallow, such as water, milk, or juice.
senses.example: Water is my favorite drink when I am thirsty.

senses.definition: To control the movement of a car, truck, or other vehicle.
senses.example: My aunt will drive us to the museum.

senses.definition: A trip in a vehicle.
senses.example: We took a drive through the hills.

senses.definition: A small amount of liquid that hangs or falls as one bit.
senses.example: A drop of water fell onto my sleeve.

senses.definition: A fall or decrease in amount, level, or position.
senses.example: By morning, we noticed a drop in temperature.

senses.definition: To let something fall, or to become lower.
senses.example: Please don’t drop the jar.

senses.definition: To take someone or something to a place and leave them or it there.
senses.example: Could we drop off my library books before soccer?

senses.definition: To fall asleep, often slowly or without meaning to.
senses.example: I started to drop off while my brother read the last page.

senses.definition: To become smaller in number, amount, or strength.
senses.example: The number of birds at the feeder began to drop off when the storm passed.

senses.definition: Not sharp at an edge or point.
senses.example: These dull scissors will not cut the cloth.

senses.definition: Not bright, clear, or interesting.
senses.example: The sky was a dull gray all afternoon.

senses.definition: To make or become less sharp, strong, or bright.
senses.example: Dust can dull the shine of a mirror.

senses.definition: A hill or ridge of sand pushed together by wind or water.
senses.example: Beach grass helped keep sand from blowing away from the dune.

senses.definition: At some time within an event or period of time.
senses.example: A dog barked during our music lesson.

senses.definition: An object that orbits the Sun, is nearly round, and shares its neighborhood with other objects of similar importance. It is not a moon.
senses.example: Pluto and Ceres are both dwarf planets.

senses.definition: How loud or soft sounds are in music and how the loudness changes.
senses.example: The conductor asked the group to watch the dynamics in the last part.

senses.definition: A line of rulers from the same family, or the stretch of time when that family rules.
senses.example: The Tang dynasty ruled China for almost three hundred years.
